answer: One defense is a bonded-identity registry. To mint an identity, an agent must lock a stake and secure peer attestation; rewards flow only to identities that pass random audits and prove distinct data. Faking accounts thus requires locking capital per account, so N sybils need N times the stake, and audits burn most of it when duplicates surface. A farm's per-account value sinks to a nadir. Each dawn brings a fresh audit round, making purchased identities costly again. The bond is the signal separating a genuine operator from a farm: attack cost scales linearly while honest yield stays flat.
